newsitem.title: POLAND: Optimus eyes matching '96 growth in '97.
newsitem.headline: Optimus eyes matching '96 growth in '97.

text.p: Polish computer maker Optimus SA expects its sales to grow this year at roughly the same rate as in 1996, the firm's president said on Tuesday.
"We plan growth of around 40 percent this year....I'm referring to sales," Roman Kluska told a news conference.
Kluska would not give a profit forecast but said he hoped the firm could maintain its 1996 growth.
In 1996 Optimus lifted net profit to 16.5 million zlotys from 9.2 million zlotys the year before. Sales rose to 500.3 million zlotys from 341.7 million zlotys in 1995.

Kluska said the firm this year would be buoyed by having installed a new computer system linking its subsidiaries, and its introduction of new product lines for the young, low-budget family customers.

Kluska said about half of its 1997 earnings could come from non-computer products such as its multi-media and internet divisions, which can take advantage of the Optimus sales and distribution network.
He said the firm's computer market share would remain at about 35 percent.
